title: Player comparison
lead: Compare startup, seeking and playback under changing delivery conditions using the same video.

items.label: Current playback checks and reference values

blocks.text: Choose the same video for each player

The default is Big Buck Bunny HLS, shared by Player Web X, Bitmovin Player 8, hls.js and Shaka Player. Startup and seek uses the same fixed 360p rendition and English audio for every player. Network change uses the same video with an adaptive ladder. You can instead enter a custom HLS or DASH URL; its initial quality is selected by each SDK and may differ.
Player Web X 10.3.1 has partial DASH support, so some custom DASH manifests may be incompatible. hls.js supports HLS; a DASH run is shown as unsupported, not as a zero-duration result.
Custom URLs are used for the current page session. The app does not save them in its browser storage or include them in result exports.

blocks.caption: Single view. Startup and seek are different intervals; the values belong to the captured run.

blocks.text: Measure and re-measure

items: Choose Startup and seek, or Network change for the default Big Buck Bunny source. Network change is disabled for custom URLs.
Select Measure. The players run one at a time; another player is not loaded during the measured playback.
Keep the tab in the foreground and read the progress for the active player.
Select Measure again to start a new run. Read its results separately from the previous run.

blocks.text: Select Stop to cancel the current measurement. Read cancellation as an outcome, not as a completed measurement.

Single view and Side by side change how the smaller video panels are displayed. Side-by-side playback is a visual preview: players share decoding and network resources. Preview values do not form a ranking or replace the separate, sequential measurements.

blocks.caption: Side by side previews concurrent playback. The graphs retain the separate sequential measurements.

blocks.text: Read the startup graph

Playback startup starts when that player’s Measure trial is accepted, before its fresh playback document is created, and ends when an advancing video frame is observed. It includes SDK import, initialization and loading. The playing event is a separate detail, not the end of this graph. Overlapping detail intervals must not be added together.

This is each player’s measurement, not the total wait from the initial button click through the full run. In Network change, Service Worker preparation finishes before that measurement starts and is excluded from the startup interval.

The values describe this run in this browser. Keep source, format, browser, cache and delivery conditions consistent when comparing. A single measurement does not establish which player is fastest in general.
Read seeking and buffer status

Seeking continues on the same loaded player. Read the displayed target and whether it was inside or outside the buffered ranges at the request. For live or limited-range media, use the valid seekable range rather than assuming a fixed position is available.

Playback after seek starts at the seek request and ends only after a frame near the target is observed and playback advances from it. The seeked event alone is not completion. If the browser cannot supply frame callbacks, the moving-frame latency is unavailable; it is not replaced by zero or another event.
Read delivery changes, quality and stalls

Network change continues playback to observe quality and stalls through the delivery-rate phases. It does not measure a seek, so the seek result stays unmeasured in this mode. Choose Startup and seek for the seek graph.

Network change is limited to the default Big Buck Bunny test source. Custom URLs support startup and seeking, but not this delivery control. A Service Worker paces readable media response bodies under one shared budget. This does not change the physical connection, network latency or cache state, and does not shape SDK downloads or license requests.

Check the control status, shaped response count, delivered bytes and skipped responses before interpreting the timeline. Some SDK requests may not pass through this control. An unsupported or skipped response does not establish that all media traffic was shaped.
Each delivery-rate phase needs newly delivered bytes during that phase. A cumulative byte count from earlier phases does not prove that a later rate was applied.

Quality changes and stalls appear only when observed. A source with one rendition cannot demonstrate adaptive quality switching, and an SDK may not expose every quality or bandwidth value. Missing observations stay missing. The configured delivery cap and a player’s estimated bandwidth are different values.
The Startup and seek timeline also includes stalls during a seek. Distinguish those waits from stalls caused by a delivery-rate change.
When an observation is missing

items: Read the status and reason: unsupported format, unavailable browser API, cancellation and playback failure are different outcomes.
No result is prefilled before measurement. Missing or failed observations are not zero-millisecond successes.
Check playback and source access before repeating a failed run; the displayed values do not bypass source or license requirements.

blocks.text: Save the observations

Save JSON keeps the measured results and safe comparison conditions. Custom source URLs are not included. Keep the outcomes and unavailable-value reasons when sharing a result; an export does not turn a failed or unsupported operation into a successful sample.
Player Web X

Player Web X uses its native Player and Source APIs alongside Bitmovin Player 8, hls.js and Shaka Player. The main Web lab uses Player v8 for configuration and API inspection; those settings and the v8 compatibility layer are separate from this comparison.
Advanced startup benchmark

The retained benchmark provides SDK import mode, configuration candidates, repeated trials, median/p95 summaries and JSON export. Its isolated startup trials are separate from the retained playback, seek and delivery timelines on Player comparison.

blocks.caption: Retained startup benchmark: SDK import and configuration candidates.

blocks.text: Evaluate settings separately from confirmation

In the advanced benchmark, candidate evaluation requires All players, the startup-settings profile and at least six trials per player. Screening varies the hls.js worker and Shaka prefetch limit, then runs new confirmation trials with the selected settings. Read the screening and confirmation phases separately; a selected candidate is not a proven optimum.

blocks.caption: Retained startup benchmark: one trial per player does not qualify for a median ranking.

blocks.text: In the advanced summary, n counts successful values for the selected metric. p95 uses sorted rank ceil(0.95 × n), so it can equal the maximum with few samples. A smallest-median label requires matching conditions and versions, equal successful counts of at least five per player, all players and no failures, cancellations or missing metric values. Ties remain ties; the label applies only to that cohort.
Save advanced benchmark results

Save JSON exports schema 2 records from the advanced benchmark. Each trial retains its conditions, outcome, device-clock start time and coarse environment snapshot. Source URLs, keys, headers, raw SDK errors and raw user-agent text are excluded. Later resizing does not change an earlier trial’s viewport record.
Recorded results belong to their original conditions

The 2026-11-01 report and the checks published with version 0.2.0 describe the earlier implementation and their recorded conditions. They are historical evidence, not measurements of the redesigned comparison or a new performance claim.
